summary: Use readable tag versions for forge release titles and ISO attachments without changing Debian package identities or website download paths.

guide.reason: The publication guide now identifies hyphenated forge filenames and matching sidecars separately from unchanged Debian-form website paths and package versions.

api.reason: Only forge presentation changes. No Controller operation, Core command, observed-state/result flow or client-facing Nex API changes; docs/API.md remains accurate and unchanged.

roadmap.reason: Release filename presentation does not change a milestone or its acceptance status.

state.reason: No new product state. Temporary forge asset hard links leave Core state, Debian identities, download paths and netinst payload URLs unchanged.

verification.method: On 2026-10-03, the new regression failed four release-candidate/development naming cases across both workflow copies before the fix. After the fix, PYTHONPATH=tests python3 -m unittest test_ci_security test_release_version test_gitea_release passed 52 tests. The test executes the actual workflow shell and real publisher against a local simulated HTTP forge for final, release-candidate and development fixtures, compares downloaded bytes and runs sha256sum -c on both sidecars. A separate disposable development smoke executed the actual .github publication step and real publisher: exit 0, title Nex Core 0.4.20-dev.247 (development), four hyphenated attachments, both downloaded checksum checks OK. Documentation structure/impact checks passed. Independent code and documentation reviewers reported no findings. The required repository privacy suite failed on personal paths embedded in unrelated core.* dump files, which were left untouched; a scoped scan of all nine changed files found no privacy findings. No hosted publication, full ISO build, installation or live release renaming was performed.
